globals.spl_root: the folder of the study on the SAS server (the one line a program sets: %LET spl_root = ...;)
globals.spl_program: the name of the program, set by %study
globals.spl_quiet: yes: no begin and end lines of the macros in the log (%LET spl_quiet = yes; before the calls)

macros.name: _spl_arg
macros.purpose: One parameter of a call that a one-call table writes into its long program: its name and its value. A parameter without a value is left out.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements that add the parameter to the arrays PN and PV of %_spl_program(begin).
macros.des: One parameter of a call in the long program of a one-call table (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: _name
parameters.description: The name of the parameter in the call; without _value also the parameter of the calling macro whose value is written

parameters.name: _value
parameters.description: A DATA step expression with the value (a text)

macros.example:
%_spl_arg(data, "&rec.")
%_spl_arg(where)

macros.name: _spl_begin
macros.purpose: The begin line of a macro in the log, with the version of the macro library; it gives the time it began, for the end line (%_spl_end). The version below is the one place of the version of the library: every header says the same.
macros.output: TEXT: the text of the time it began (seconds); the line NOTE: [describe] begins (Sapling macro library 1.1.0). in the log, unless SPL_QUIET is yes (a global macro variable: %LET spl_quiet = yes; before the calls keeps the log short).
macros.des: The begin line of a macro in the log

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

macros.example: %_spl_begin(describe)

macros.name: _spl_call
macros.purpose: One call of a macro in the long program of a one-call table: the parameters given by %_spl_arg since the last call, one per line, the equal signs under each other.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements that write the call to the file of the long program and start the next list of parameters.
macros.des: One call of a macro in the long program of a one-call table (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the macro called, without the percent sign

macros.example: %_spl_call(freq)

macros.name: _spl_chars
macros.purpose: The character variables among some variables of a data set (their names, separated by blanks). The statistics macros give them one length ($200) in their results, so that results stack without a cut value.
macros.output: TEXT: the names of the character variables among VARS, separated by blanks (a variable not in DATA is left out).
macros.des: The character variables among some variables of a data set

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set (data set options after it are ignored)

parameters.name: vars
parameters.description: The variables

macros.example: %_spl_chars(adae, TRT01A AEBODSYS AEDECOD AVISITN)

macros.name: _spl_csv
macros.purpose: Write a data set as a CSV file: a line with the names of the variables, then one line per row (a DATA step; values with a comma or a quote are quoted).
macros.output: FILE:  a line with the names of the variables, then one line per row.
macros.des: Write a data set as a CSV file (DATA steps)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set (data set options such as KEEP= are allowed)

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The CSV file to write

macros.example: %_spl_csv(data=l14_3_1(KEEP=usubjid aedecod), file=&spl_out./listings/l14_3_1.csv)

macros.name: _spl_empty
macros.purpose: The result of a statistics macro when no record qualifies: the result shape without a row, and a NOTE that says so. A procedure never runs on no record, so the log has no error of one.
macros.output: OUT: KEEP, ADD, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT and no row; the line NOTE: [macro] No data qualified ... in the log.
macros.des: The result shape without a row: no data qualified

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: The group variables of the result (BY, WITHIN)

parameters.name: macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: like
parameters.description: The records (without a row): the types and lengths of the group variables

parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Character group variables the records do not have (VERSUS)

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The result to write

macros.example: %_spl_empty(macro=cox, out=&out., like=_cox_records, keep=&by. &within., add=versus)

macros.name: _spl_end
macros.purpose: The end line of a macro in the log: its run time since its begin line (%_spl_begin), and with debug=yes that its work data sets are kept.
macros.output: LOG: NOTE: [describe] ends after 0.42 seconds. in the log, unless SPL_QUIET is yes; with debug=yes always the line that names the kept work data sets.
macros.des: The end line of a macro in the log

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: _start
parameters.description: The time it began (%_spl_begin)

parameters.name: _debug
parameters.description: The debug= of the calling macro

macros.example: %_spl_end(describe, &t0., &debug.)

macros.name: _spl_figure_attrs
macros.purpose: The look of the groups of a figure: an attribute map (DATTRMAP=) that gives each value of the group variable a colour, a marker and a line pattern, in the order of the columns of %columns (columns=; a value not in it after them), else in the order the values come in the data. Eight colours safe for colour blindness (Okabe and Ito, without the yellow, and a grey), each with another marker and line pattern, so that groups differ in black and white too; a ninth group starts the list again. ID grp has all attributes; ID grpcol the colours only, solid lines (an error bar; a marker of its own, such as the censoring mark: give it to a copy of the group variable, as SGPLOT takes one ID per variable). The data get _ORDER, the place of their group.
macros.output: OUT: the attribute map: ID, VALUE, _ORDER and the attributes; DATA: data= with _ORDER.
macros.des: The colours, markers and line patterns of the groups of a figure

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The rows of the figure: they get _ORDER

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: The columns of %columns (COL, COLVALUE)

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The group variable

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The attribute map

macros.example: %_spl_figure_attrs(data=_kmplot_plot, columns=&columns., var=&by., out=_kmplot_attrs)

macros.name: _spl_figure_close
macros.purpose: Close the destinations of a figure (%_spl_figure_open) and set back what it changed: the RTF file closed, LISTING closed and opened again (its style LISTING) when it was open before, the options of ODS GRAPHICS reset.
macros.output: CODE: the ODS statements that close the destinations.
macros.des: Close the destinations of a figure and set back what it changed

parameters.name: listing
parameters.description: yes: LISTING was open before the figure

macros.example: %_spl_figure_close(listing=&listing.)

macros.name: _spl_figure_dodge
macros.purpose: Move the groups a little apart on a numeric x axis, so that their error bars do not overlap: _XPLOT = x + (_ORDER - (G + 1) / 2) * STEP, G the number of groups, STEP the smaller of half the smallest distance of two x values divided by G - 1 and 3% of the range of x. The x of the data stays as it is. With offset= the room the axis needs at each end, so that the outer groups are not cut at the edge of the plot.
macros.output: DATA: data= with _XPLOT; with offset= that macro variable.
macros.des: Move the groups of a figure a little apart on the x axis

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The rows of the figure, with _ORDER (%_spl_figure_attrs)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The numeric x variable

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: A macro variable of the caller: it gets the offset of each end of the axis (OFFSETMIN=, OFFSETMAX= of COLAXIS), a fraction of its length

macros.example: %_spl_figure_dodge(data=_meanplot_plot, x=x, offset=xoff)

macros.name: _spl_figure_label
macros.purpose: The label of an axis, as a text in quotes: the text given (in quotes, or put in quotes), else the label of the variable, else its name.
macros.output: TEXT: the label in double quotes.
macros.des: The label of an axis, in quotes

parameters.name: _data
parameters.description: The data set

parameters.name: _var
parameters.description: The variable of the axis

parameters.name: _text
parameters.description: The text given, or nothing

macros.example: %_spl_figure_label(&data., &time., %SUPERQ(xlabel))

macros.name: _spl_figure_nodata
macros.purpose: No record qualified for a figure: out= in the shape of the figure with no row, the NOTE No data qualified, and the figure that says so (a blank plot with the text, in the PNG and the RTF of file=, under the titles of the program).
macros.output: OUT: no row; FILE: <file>.png and <file>.rtf with the text.
macros.des: The figure and the result when no record qualified

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: The variables of like= kept in out=

parameters.name: macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: like
parameters.description: The records, without a row

parameters.name: chars
parameters.description: Character variables of out= ($200)

parameters.name: nums
parameters.description: Numeric variables of out=

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The output without its extension

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The width of the figure

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The height of the figure

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The result to write (none: no data set)

macros.example:
%_spl_figure_nodata(
     keep   = &by.
   , macro  = kmplot
   , like   = _kmplot_records
   , chars  = kind
   , nums   = x y n censored
   , file   = &file.
   , width  = &width.
   , height = &height.
   , out    = &out.
 )

macros.name: _spl_figure_open
macros.purpose: Open the destinations of one figure: the PNG image (the LISTING destination with GPATH=, 300 dpi, image name and size from ODS GRAPHICS) and the RTF file with the figure on a page (the titles and footnotes of the program as text of the page: NOGTITLE NOGFOOTNOTE). The PNG carries the titles and the footnotes in the image (LISTING draws them in the graph, as SAS does by default), so a PNG alone says what it is. Both use the style HTMLBLUE: tick values 9pt, axis labels and legend 10pt, titles 11pt. It notes in the macro variable named by state= whether LISTING was open, for %_spl_figure_close.
macros.output: CODE: the ODS statements that open the destinations.
macros.des: Open the PNG and RTF destinations of a figure

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The output without its extension: <file>.png and <file>.rtf

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The width of the figure

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The height of the figure

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The name of a local macro variable of the caller: yes when LISTING was open, else no

macros.example: %_spl_figure_open(file=&file., width=&width., height=&height., state=LISTING)

macros.name: _spl_figure_outpar
macros.purpose: The drawing parameters of a figure macro as a data set (its outpar=): one row per parameter in the order of the signature, PARAMETER its name in lower case and VALUE its value as the macro draws it (given, from par=, the default, or made by the macro: the label of an axis, the format of the ticks). par= of a later call reads it back.
macros.output: DATA: out= with PARAMETER ($32) and VALUE ($500).
macros.des: Write the drawing parameters of a figure macro as a data set

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: The drawing parameters of the caller, in their order (names= of %_spl_figure_par)

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The data set to write; blank: none

macros.example: %_spl_figure_outpar(names=&drawn., out=&outpar.)

macros.name: _spl_figure_par
macros.purpose: The parameters of a figure macro, before its checks. With plot= (draw the out= of a call again): data= is not given, plot= has the variables of out=, and each parameter of the computation that has a value gets a NOTE (it is not used). With par= (the outpar= of a call): each drawing parameter that the call leaves blank gets the VALUE of its row; a row that names no drawing parameter is an error. Then each parameter still blank gets its default from draw= or compute=. So a value in the call wins over a row of par=, and a row of par= over the default: the defaults of these parameters are here, not in the signature of the macro.
macros.output: LOG: one ERROR with its fix for a wrong plot= or par=, a NOTE for each parameter not used. The local macro variables of the caller: the parameters set from par= and from the defaults, state= and names=.
macros.des: Read par= and the defaults of a figure macro, and check plot=

parameters.name: macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: draw
parameters.description: Its drawing parameters in the order of its signature, each as name or name=default

parameters.name: compute
parameters.description: Its parameters of the computation that plot= does not use, each as name or name=default

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The variables of its out= that plot= must have

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: The name of a local macro variable of the caller: the names of the drawing parameters

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The name of a local macro variable of the caller: 1 when the parameters are right, else 0

macros.example:
%_spl_figure_par(
     macro   = kmplot
   , draw    = columns by panel atrisk=yes xlabel ylabel="Survival (%)" file
   , compute = where time cnsr=CNSR
   , shape   = kind x y lower upper n censored
   , names   = drawn
   , state   = ok
 )

macros.name: _spl_folder
macros.purpose: Make the folder of a file the macro writes, and each folder above it that is missing, with a NOTE that names the folder made. A path that starts with ~ is in the home folder. Nothing is made when the folder is there or the file has no folder.
macros.output: LOG: NOTE: [print] made the folder ~/study/out/tlf. for a folder it made; a WARNING when the folder cannot be made.
macros.des: Make the folder of a file and the folders above it that are missing

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: _file
parameters.description: The file the macro writes: a path

macros.example: %_spl_folder(print, %SUPERQ(file).rtf)

macros.name: _spl_levels
macros.purpose: The planned categories of some variables as rows: every combination of their values, by DO loops. A character variable gets the length $200.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements: LENGTH of the character variables ($200), then DO loops that output every combination of the planned values (DO BNRIND = ...; DO ANRIND = ...; OUTPUT; END; END;); with order= also the place of each value in its list.
macros.des: The planned categories of some variables as rows (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set of the variables (it tells which ones are character)

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Each variable followed by its values: a text in quotes, a number without

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: A prefix: the place of each value in its list as the variables <prefix>1, <prefix>2 ... (one for each variable, in the order of levels=)

macros.example: %_spl_levels(levels=bnrind 'LOW' 'NORMAL' 'HIGH' anrind 'LOW' 'NORMAL' 'HIGH', data=adlbc)

macros.name: _spl_need
macros.purpose: Check the parameters a macro needs: each must have a value, and a data set of data=, denom=, columns= or from= must exist. For each one that does not it writes one line that names the parameter and the fix: ERROR: [describe] data= is required: give data=<value> ... ERROR: [describe] data=adsx does not exist: give data= ... It gives 1 when all are there, 0 when one is not: the caller then stops (%RETURN).
macros.output: TEXT: 1 or 0, as text.
macros.des: Check the parameters a macro needs

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro (for the message)

parameters.name: _params
parameters.description: The names of its parameters that must have a value

macros.example: %_spl_need(describe, data var by out)

macros.name: _spl_nobs
macros.purpose: The number of rows of a data set (with the WHERE= of its data set options, when it has one); 0 when the data set does not exist.
macros.output: TEXT: the number, as text.
macros.des: The number of rows of a data set

parameters.name: _data
parameters.description: The data set

macros.example: %_spl_nobs(_describe_values)

macros.name: _spl_oneof
macros.purpose: Check that the value of a parameter is one of a list (in any case). When it is not it writes one line that names the parameter and the fix: ERROR: [cox] ties=fast is not one of efron breslow exact ... It gives 1 or 0: the caller then stops (%RETURN).
macros.output: TEXT: 1 or 0, as text.
macros.des: Check that a parameter is one of a list

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro (for the message)

parameters.name: _param
parameters.description: The parameter

parameters.name: _list
parameters.description: Its values, separated by blanks

macros.example: %_spl_oneof(cox, ties, efron breslow exact discrete)

macros.name: _spl_pairlist
macros.purpose: The pairs of groups of a parameter as rows: _K (the place of the pair), _A (the group) and _B (the group it is compared with). The pairs are separated by #, one pair per line, the first group against the second; a value with a blank or a hyphen is in quotes: pairs = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo" # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo" The form of version 1.0 is still read: "A"-"B" "C"-"D" (no #, every item a pair joined by a hyphen outside quotes).
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements: one row (OUTPUT) per pair with _K, _A and _B ($200).
macros.des: The pairs of groups of a parameter as rows _K _A _B (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: The parameter of the calling macro that holds the pairs (pairs, family)

macros.example: %_spl_pairlist(list=pairs)

macros.name: _spl_pairs
macros.purpose: The differences of the pairs of groups asked for, from the table Diffs of PROC MIXED (it has each pair once, in one direction). It computes nothing: a difference the other way round is the same difference with its sign and its limits turned.
macros.output: OUT: WITHIN, BY (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl, pval: one row per pair asked for (in each group of WITHIN).
macros.des: The differences of the pairs of groups asked for, from the table Diffs of a procedure

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: a character variable

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: The variables of the separate models (BY groups of PROC MIXED)

parameters.name: diffs
parameters.description: The Diffs table (the group in BY, the group it is compared with in _BY)

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: The records of the model (for the groups and their order)

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of ORDER (else of the values); or the pairs separated by #, the group first, then the group it is compared with (%_spl_pairlist reads them, and the form "A"-"B" of 1.0)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: A numeric variable of the records with one value per group

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The data set: WITHIN, BY (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl, pval

macros.example:
%_spl_pairs(
     by      = trt01p
   , within  =
   , diffs   = _lsmeans_diffs
   , records = _lsmeans_records
   , pairs   = all
   , order   = trt01pn
   , out     = _lsmeans_pairs
 )

macros.name: _spl_program
macros.purpose: The fixed parts of the DATA step with which a one-call table writes its long program: begin (the file and the variables), records (the population and the records, from the parameters ADSL, POP, DATA, WHERE and NAME of the calling macro), table (the %table call, from BY, ORDER, TOTAL, FORMAT, FILE, NAME and DEBUG, with the TITLE and FOOTNOTE statements of TITLE and FOOTNOTE before it and their clearing after it), titles and untitled (those statements alone), end (the routine that writes a call). It computes nothing.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements. It reads the macro variables REC (the records the calls read), POPN (the data set with the N of the columns), DS and NAMES of the calling macro.
macros.des: The fixed parts of the long program of a one-call table (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: _part
parameters.description: begin, names, label, records, table, titles, untitled or end

parameters.name: _var
parameters.description: With label: the variable of the block, in lower case

macros.example:
%_spl_program(begin)
%_spl_program(records)
%_spl_program(table)
%_spl_program(end)

macros.name: _spl_quote
macros.purpose: The value of a parameter as a text in single quotes, for a DATA step: each single quote in it doubled, nothing in it resolved. The code the macro writes holds the value itself (SYMGET would read it when the step runs), so that the flat program of sapling sas run --flat (the code without a macro) has it too. An empty value gives a blank text.
macros.output: TEXT: a text in single quotes: 'Age (years)', '"A" "B" # "C" "B"'.
macros.des: The value of a parameter as a text in single quotes (DATA step code)

parameters.name: _param
parameters.description: The name of the parameter (label, pairs)

macros.example: %_spl_quote(label)

macros.name: _spl_rows
macros.purpose: The result shape: one row per statistic of the row just read. Each statistic is a numeric variable of the same name (n, mean, pval ...); the row gets STAT (its name), VALUE (its number), PATTERN and TEXT (the number as printed, %_spl_text: a p value, pval or padj, never as 0 or 1).
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements: one row per statistic with STAT, VALUE and TEXT. The default patterns: XX for n, events, min, max; XX.X for mean, median, q1, q3, lsmean, diff, estimate, lcl, ucl; (XX.X%) for pct; X.XXX for pval; XX.XX for sd, se, lsmean_se, diff_se and any other statistic.
macros.des: The result shape: one row per statistic (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: missing
parameters.description: The text of a statistic without a value (default blank; %km gives NE: not estimable)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics in their order, each with its pattern (mean="XX.X") or without (the default pattern of the statistic below)

macros.example: %_spl_rows(stats=n="XX" mean="XX.X" sd)

macros.name: _spl_stackpairs
macros.purpose: The records of each pair of groups asked for, one under the other: the pair (_PAIR), its group (_A) and the group it is compared with (_B), and the side of each record (_SIDE: 1 in _A, 2 in _B). A procedure then runs BY _PAIR _A _B on the 2 groups of each pair, the group first. It computes nothing.
macros.output: OUT: the records of each pair with _PAIR, _A, _B and _SIDE (1 in _A, 2 in _B), sorted by them. The macro variable PAIRSOK of the caller: 1, or 0 when a pair names a group that no record has (an error in the log).
macros.des: The records of each pair of groups asked for, one under the other

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: a character variable

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: The records (one per subject)

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of ORDER (else of the values); or the pairs separated by #, the group first, then the group it is compared with (%_spl_pairlist reads them, and the form "A"-"B" of 1.0)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: A numeric variable of the records with one value per group

parameters.name: macro
parameters.description: The macro that calls (for the message)

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The data set: the records of each pair with _PAIR, _A, _B, _SIDE, sorted by them

macros.example:
%_spl_stackpairs(
     macro   = ttest
   , records = _ttest_records
   , by      = trt01p
   , pairs   = all
   , order   = trt01pn
   , out     = _ttest_pairs
 )

macros.name: _spl_text
macros.purpose: The text of a number by its pattern. A pattern shows one number as one group of X: XX, XX.X, (XX.X%), (N=XX). The number is rounded (ROUND) to the decimals of the X group, right aligned in its width and put in its place; the text is trimmed. A p value never prints as 0 or 1: rounded to 0 it is < and the smallest step (X.XXX: <0.001), rounded to 1 it is > and one step less (>0.999). The number is unchanged.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements: TEXT is the number of VALUE as its PATTERN shows it (9.46 with (XX.X%) gives ( 9.5%); 86 with (N=XX) gives (N=86); 3 with XX gives 3; a p value 0.00004 with X.XXX gives <0.001).
macros.des: The text of a number by its pattern (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The numeric variable

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The character variable with the pattern

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The character variable to write (blank when the number is missing)

parameters.name: pvalue
parameters.description: A condition that is true when the number is a p value (STAT IN ('pval' 'padj'))

macros.example:
%_spl_text(
       value   = value
     , pattern = pattern
     , text    = text
     , pvalue  = stat IN ('pval' 'padj')
   )

macros.name: _spl_total
macros.purpose: The name of the group of all groups together, from total=: nothing for no, Total for yes, else the text in quotes.
macros.output: TEXT: nothing for no (or empty), Total for yes, else the text of the quotes.
macros.des: The name of the group of all groups together, from total=

parameters.name: total
parameters.description: The value of total= (no, yes, or a name in quotes)

macros.example: %_spl_total(%SUPERQ(total))

macros.name: _spl_vars
macros.purpose: Check that the variables of some parameters are variables of a data set. For each one that is not it writes one line that names the parameter and the fix: ERROR: [describe] var=AGEX is not a variable of adsl: give ... It gives 1 when all are there, 0 when one is not: the caller then stops (%RETURN). A data set that cannot be opened is the business of %_spl_need. With _also (the subjects adsl= of a one-call table, whose variables go to the records) a variable of either data set is there.
macros.output: TEXT: 1 or 0, as text.
macros.des: Check that variables are in a data set

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro (for the message)

parameters.name: _data
parameters.description: The parameter that names the data set (data, denom)

parameters.name: _params
parameters.description: The parameters whose values are variables of it

parameters.name: _also
parameters.description: The parameter that names a second data set where the variables may be (adsl)

macros.example:
%_spl_vars(describe, data, var by)
%_spl_vars(table_ae, data, var by, adsl)

macros.name: _spl_windows
macros.purpose: The rows of windows= (or visits=) of a call as a data set: one row per window, the rows of the call separated by #, the values of a row by blanks, a text in quotes, a missing number as a period.
macros.output: DATA: _out, one row per window in the order of the call. The macro variable ROWSOK of the caller: 1, or 0 when a row has not its number of values (an error in the log).

macros.name: layout
macros.purpose: The display data set of a table: one row per printed line, as the shells have it. The label of a block, the levels of its groups indented by two blanks each (a term under its class, a visit under its parameter, vs B under A), the statistics of a line put in the template of the line; one column per group with its header and N from %columns, and the column All groups for a p-value of all groups; the p-value of each category (a test of each term, a block of the same label) stands in the row of its category. A category that format= names shows its label. It computes nothing: every number is the TEXT of a result. The line table (Step 3), line: label = template: 0 a category of a frequency block = {n} {pct} {events}; 1 n = {n}; 2 Events = {events}; 2.5 Patient-years = {exposure}; 3 Mean (SD) = {mean} ({sd}) [{se}] (se only: Mean (SE); sd and se: Mean (SD) [SE]); 4 Median = {median}; 5 Q1, Q3 = {q1}, {q3}; 6 Min, Max = {min}, {max}; 7 LS mean (SE) = {lsmean} ({lsmean_se}); 8 Difference (SE) = {diff} ({diff_se}); 9 the estimate by its STAT (hr Hazard ratio, or Odds ratio, irr Rate ratio, rd Risk difference, rr Relative risk, rate Rate per 100 patient-years, else Estimate) = {estimate}; 10 Confidence interval = ({lcl}, {ucl}); 11 p-value = {pval}; 11.5 Adjusted p-value = {padj}; 12 any other STAT, labelled by it = {value}. A part that is missing leaves out its piece of the template with its brackets or its comma (a confidence interval without its upper limit prints the lower limit alone); a TEXT that has the brackets of its piece already is not bracketed twice; the counts of a frequency block are right aligned to the widest count. With setup= it also keeps the %print call of OUT in a global macro variable of that name: %print(&name.) prints the display data set again after a change. The setup holds data=, by=, var=, together= and label= (row=" " and the labels of label=), and rows=, file= and nodata= when they are given here. A parameter that is not in the setup is added after it: %print(&name., file=...); one that is in it cannot be given twice (SAS stops a call with a keyword given twice): give it to %layout again, or write the %print call. With page= (a BY variable of the results, such as SEX) the table is one page per value: the page variable is no level of the rows, each page starts with its first block, and the header of each column on a page has the N of that page (%columns with the same page=).

Cn (the cells, labelled with the header of their column) and C99 (All groups: only when a result has a p-value of all groups). With page=: also the page variable (with its format of format=) and HEAD_C1 ... HEAD_Cn, the header of each column on its page; C1 ... Cn are labelled with the column value. SETUP: with setup=, the global macro variable of that name: the parameters of %print for OUT, such as data=t14_2_1_display, by=row, var=c:, together=grp, label=row=" " (a NOTE in the log shows it); print with %print(&name.).

ODS wraps and pages the RTF; the rows of one TOGETHER value stay on one page of the listing when they fit in ROWS. macros.name: termflags
macros.purpose: The flag of each row of occurrence data for every subject: one record per subject of DENOM (with its group BY) and per term (each combination of TERMS in the records), FLAG "Y" when the subject has a record of the term and "N" when not. With threshold= only the terms whose percent of the subjects of a group reaches it in at least one group. It computes no statistic: %risk then compares the groups on FLAG within each term (within=TERMS), one record per subject, the subjects of the group the denominator.

parameters.name: denom

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use, a condition in parentheses

macros.name: tte
macros.purpose: One time-to-event parameter in one call: for each subject the first event, else the latest censoring. With end= an at-risk period from START to END: only the events and censorings in it count, else the subject is censored at the end of the period.
macros.proven: the fixtures of the step kinds tte and tte.period (src/adam_steps.ts; node tools/adam_steps_sas.ts); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: one record per subject with an event, a censoring or (with end=) a period: the variables of SUBJECTS, PARAMCD, ADT, CNSR, AVAL (ADT - START + 1), ATM (with time=) and the values above, in the order of SUBJECTS. With end= a subject without START or without END gets no record and a WARNING that names it (USUBJID=); a subject whose START is after its END gets no record. Two records of a subject in SUBJECTS are an ERROR.
macros.des: One time-to-event parameter: the first event, else the latest censoring (PROC SORT)

parameters.name: subjects
parameters.description: One record per subject (USUBJID) with START (and END). The result keeps its variables: it must not have ADT, CNSR, AVAL or the values below.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: The records the events come from: a data set

parameters.name: censors
parameters.description: The records of the censorings: the latest date in the period (on one date the last record). Default: SUBJECTS.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Which records of EVENTS are events: a condition. Default: all.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The date of an event, a variable of EVENTS (missing: no event)

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: The time of an event (seconds since midnight), a variable of EVENTS, for the start day

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Variables of EVENTS that order the events of one date (a missing value last). Default: the order of the data.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The start of the period and the origin of AVAL, a date of SUBJECTS

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: The time of the start, of SUBJECTS: on the start day an event counts unless both times are there and the event time is before it

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The end of the at-risk period, a date of SUBJECTS. Without END: no period, every date counts, a date before START is START (as admiral).

parameters.name: censor_date
parameters.description: The date of a censoring, of CENSORS (or of SUBJECTS)

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: SRCSEQ of an event: a variable of EVENTS. Default: missing.

parameters.name: adtf
parameters.description: ADTF of an event: the flag of its date, a variable of EVENTS

parameters.name: atmf
parameters.description: ATMF of an event: the flag of its time, a variable of EVENTS

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Other variables of the record taken, in EVENTS and CENSORS both (the values of the rows that the program stacked before the call)

parameters.name: censor_cnsr
parameters.description: CNSR of a censoring: a number, or a variable of CENSORS

parameters.name: end_cnsr
parameters.description: CNSR at the end of the period

parameters.name: censor_desc
parameters.description: EVNTDESC of a censoring: a text in quotes, or a variable

parameters.name: censor_source
parameters.description: SRCDOM of a censoring of SUBJECTS and of the end of the period, in quotes; SRCVAR is then the name of CENSOR_DATE (of END)

parameters.name: end_desc
parameters.description: EVNTDESC at the end of the period

parameters.name: event_desc
parameters.description: EVNTDESC of an event: a text in quotes, or a variable of EVENTS

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: SRCDOM of an event, in quotes; SRCVAR is then the name of DATE

parameters.name: paramcd
parameters.description: PARAMCD, in quotes

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The result (see Output)

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _tte_*

macros.example:
%tte(
     subjects      = work.adsl
   , events        = adam.adlb
   , event         = paramcd IN ('ALT', 'AST') AND r2a1hi >= 3
   , date          = adt
   , priority      = paramcd
   , start         = trtsdt
   , end           = dcutdt
   , censor_date   = dcutdt
   , seq           = aseq
   , censor_desc   = "Cutoff date"
   , censor_source = "ADSL"
   , event_desc    = "ALT/AST >= 3x ULN"

   , out           = work.dil3x
 )
